discovery: The jamming transition: a unifying framework for rigidity and flow in disordered matter
subfield: Soft condensed matter and statistical physics of disordered systems
motivation: Liu and Nagel proposed that glasses, granular packings, foams, emulsions and colloids lose or acquire rigidity through a common jamming transition, controlled by density, temperature and stress. Their jamming phase diagram (1998), and the identification with O'Hern of point J in frictionless sphere packings (2002-2003), turned a messy many-body problem into a clear critical point with isostaticity, power-law scaling of elastic moduli and excess low-frequency vibrational modes. This picture explains the anomalous vibrational properties and boson peak of amorphous solids, the onset of plasticity and yielding, and the rheology of dense suspensions. It has been confirmed by experiments and simulations across physics, materials science, chemical engineering and biology, including tissue mechanics. Their later work on disordered mechanical metamaterials and learning in physical networks shows the continuing fertility of these ideas. Theirs is a deep conceptual contribution to the physics of disordered matter.
